request.spec:
A person's name must be unique on the sheet, comparing without regard to case and ignoring
spaces before and after the name. Names are stored with those surrounding spaces removed and
shown that way. Adding or editing a person to a name already in use is refused with an error on
the form, and nothing is saved.

agent.result_text:
I've made person names unique on each sheet, and the acceptance test passes when run with `bin/e2e`.

- **Stored data** (`db/migration/V4__person_name_unique.sql`): existing names have their surrounding spaces removed. A new `name_key` column holds the name in lower case, with a unique index on sheet and `name_key`. The database itself now rejects a duplicate.
- **Server** (`PersonService`): when a person is added or edited, the name is stored with the outer spaces removed. Before saving, the server checks whether anyone else on the sheet already has that name, ignoring case. If so, it refuses with a "conflict" error and saves nothing. A person can still be saved under their own name with different capitals. If two users take the same name at the same moment, the database index catches it and they get the same refusal instead of a generic failure.
- **Front end** (`people-api.ts`): that refusal shows on the person form as "That name is already in use on this sheet." A refused edit leaves the editor open.

The migration will fail if a sheet already holds two names that differ only in capitals or spaces, because the unique index can't be created. Today that can't happen: the database is in memory and starts empty on every run. It would matter if the app ever ran against a database that keeps its data.
